steps.name: Project scaffolding and .gitignore
steps.description:
Set up the three new top-level directories and their base config files.

- `.gitignore` already updated (node_modules/, dist/, .wrangler/, .cache/, *.tsbuildinfo) — verify it's correct
- Create `worker/` with `package.json` (wrangler, typescript deps), `tsconfig.json`, `wrangler.toml` (D1 binding named DB, routes for mydomain.dev)
- Create `worker/schema.sql` with the `labels` D1 table definition (id TEXT PK, slug TEXT UNIQUE, latitude REAL, longitude REAL, created_at TEXT, source TEXT, metadata_json TEXT)
- Create `pi/` directory with `requirements.txt` (fastapi, uvicorn[standard], requests, pydantic; RPi.GPIO listed as optional/commented)
- Create `web/` directory placeholder
- Verify: `npx tsc --noEmit` from worker/, ensure wrangler.toml is valid

steps.name: Cloudflare Worker — slug generation, DB helpers, POST /api/labels
steps.description:
Implement the core label creation endpoint in the Cloudflare Worker.

Files:
- `worker/src/slug.ts` — generates a 9-char slug from [A-Za-z0-9] using `crypto.getRandomValues`; exported as `generateSlug()`
- `worker/src/db.ts` — TypeScript types for the D1 `labels` row; thin helper for typed D1 queries
- `worker/src/routes/labels.ts` — handles `POST /api/labels`:
  - Auth: check `x-api-key` header against `env.API_KEY` secret; return 401 if missing/wrong
  - Validate: latitude ∈ [-90,90], longitude ∈ [-180,180]; return 400 if invalid
  - Generate UUID via `crypto.randomUUID()` for id
  - Generate slug, retry on UNIQUE constraint violation (up to 5 attempts)
  - Insert into D1, set created_at as ISO-8601 UTC string
  - Return 201: `{ id, slug, url: 'https://mydomain.dev/t/{slug}', createdAt }`
  - Return 500 on DB failure

Verify: `npx tsc --noEmit` passes

steps.name: Cloudflare Worker — GET /t/:slug, GET /api/labels/:slug, main router
steps.description:
Complete the Worker with the resolve route, JSON lookup, and main entry point.

Files:
- `worker/src/routes/resolve.ts` — handles `GET /t/:slug`:
  - Lookup slug in D1
  - Found: return HTML page showing slug, latitude, longitude, createdAt
  - Not found: return 404 HTML page
- `worker/src/routes/labels.ts` — extend with `GET /api/labels/:slug`:
  - Return JSON: `{ id, slug, latitude, longitude, createdAt, source }` or 404 JSON
- `worker/src/index.ts` — main fetch handler:
  - Route `POST /api/labels` → labels handler
  - Route `GET /api/labels/:slug` → labels handler
  - Route `GET /t/:slug` → resolve handler
  - All other routes → 404

Verify: `npx tsc --noEmit` passes; `npx wrangler dev` smoke test with curl for all three routes

steps.name: Pi Service — config, GPS store, POST /gps, GET /health
steps.description:
Build the core Pi service foundation.

Files:
- `pi/config.py` — reads all values from env vars with documented defaults:
  - BACKEND_URL (https://mydomain.dev)
  - API_KEY (required, no default)
  - SOURCE_ID (pi-01)
  - GPS_STALE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS (60)
  - PI_PORT (8000)
  - GPIO_PIN (17)
  - PRINTER_HOST (required)
  - PRINTER_PORT (9100)
- `pi/gps_store.py` — thread-safe in-memory GPS state:
  - Dataclass with latitude, longitude, received_at fields
  - threading.Lock for thread safety
  - `update(lat, lon)` and `get()` methods
- `pi/main.py` — FastAPI app:
  - `POST /gps`: validate coords (lat ∈ [-90,90], lon ∈ [-180,180]), store in gps_store, return `{ ok: true, storedAt: ISO-8601 }`
  - `GET /health`: return `{ ok: true, hasGps: bool, latestGpsAgeSeconds: float }`

Verify: `uvicorn main:app --port 8000`, curl POST /gps and GET /health

steps.name: Pi Service — ZPL generation and printer module
steps.description:
Implement local ZPL generation and raw printer sending.

Files:
- `pi/zpl.py` — pure function `generate_zpl(url: str) -> str`:
  - Returns ZPL string with ^XA...^XZ
  - Uses ^BQN,2,{size} for QR code
  - Centers QR on label (609x406 dot default, same as existing generate_zpl logic)
  - No external dependencies
- `pi/printer.py` — `send_to_printer(zpl: str, host: str, port: int) -> None`:
  - Opens raw TCP socket to printer (Zebra uses port 9100 by default)
  - Sends ZPL bytes
  - Raises exception on failure (caller handles PRINTER_SEND_FAILED logging)
- `pi/tests/test_zpl.py` — unit tests:
  - Verify generate_zpl output starts with ^XA, ends with ^XZ
  - Verify URL appears in output
  - Verify ^BQN command present

Verify: `python -m pytest pi/tests/test_zpl.py`

steps.name: Pi Service — print flow, GPIO handler, POST /print endpoint
steps.description:
Implement the critical print workflow, GPIO button handler, and /print endpoint.

Files:
- `pi/print_flow.py` — async `run_print_flow()` with `asyncio.Lock` concurrency guard:
  - Step 1: Check GPS exists → log NO_GPS_AVAILABLE, abort if missing
  - Step 2: Check age ≤ GPS_STALE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS → log GPS_STALE, abort if stale
  - Step 3: POST to backend /api/labels with x-api-key, lat, lon, source → log BACKEND_REQUEST_FAILED on exception
  - Step 4: Validate response contains `url` field → log BACKEND_INVALID_RESPONSE if missing
  - Step 5: Call generate_zpl(url) locally
  - Step 6: Call send_to_printer(zpl) → log PRINTER_SEND_FAILED on exception
  - Step 7: Log success with slug/url and coordinates
  - Structured log format: timestamp, event type, relevant data
- `pi/gpio_handler.py`:
  - Try to import RPi.GPIO; if ImportError, log warning and skip GPIO setup
  - Setup GPIO_PIN in BCM mode with bouncetime debounce (300ms)
  - Callback calls `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(run_print_flow(), loop)`
  - `setup(loop)` and `cleanup()` functions
- `pi/main.py` — extend with:
  - `POST /print` endpoint: calls run_print_flow(), returns `{ ok: true }` or error
  - Lifespan handler: setup GPIO on startup, cleanup on shutdown

Verify: `uvicorn main:app --port 8000`, POST /print with no GPS (expect NO_GPS_AVAILABLE log), with stale GPS (expect GPS_STALE log)

steps.name: Mobile GPS web page
steps.description:
Build the self-contained mobile GPS sender page.

File: `web/index.html` — single HTML file, no build step, no frameworks:
- Pi IP configurable via `?pi=<host:port>` URL query param; also editable via in-page text input
- `navigator.geolocation.watchPosition` for continuous updates
- On each position update: POST `{ latitude, longitude, timestamp }` to `http://<pi-ip>/gps`
- UI displays:
  - Current latitude / longitude
  - Last successful send time
  - Status badge: 'waiting', 'sending', 'success', 'error'
  - Error message if send fails
- Handles geolocation permission denial gracefully with clear error message
- Mobile-friendly layout (viewport meta, readable font sizes)

Verify: open in Chrome, grant geolocation, check network tab for POST to Pi /gps

steps.name: Final integration check and report
steps.description:
Verify all three systems end-to-end and write the completion report.

- Worker: run `npx tsc --noEmit` from `worker/`, confirm no type errors
- Worker: run `npx wrangler dev` and smoke test all routes with curl
- Pi: run `uvicorn main:app --port 8000`, smoke test POST /gps, GET /health, POST /print
- Pi: run `python -m pytest pi/tests/` if tests exist
- Web: open `web/index.html` in browser, verify geolocation prompt and status UI
- Update `plan.md` marking all steps [x]
- Write `.zenflow/tasks/new-task-4118/report.md` describing:
  - What was implemented
  - How each part was tested
  - Any issues or trade-offs encountered
  - Setup instructions for each component (wrangler deploy, pi service startup, web page usage)
